title: BDL Basic Circular No. 3: KYC Form for Cash Transactions
text:
Basic Circular No. 3 addressed to Financial Institutions
And also to Specialized Lending Entities (Comptoirs), Exchange Institutions, and
Electronic Payment Services Providers
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025, relating to the KYC
Form for Cash Transactions1.
Beirut, on 14 November 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
1- This title was amended pursuant to Article 1 of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026
(Intermediate Circular No. 761) that comes into force as of 30 June 2026.

Basic Decision No. 13769
KYC Form for Cash Transactions1
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, in particular Articles 70 and 174 thereof;
Pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 44 of 24 November 2015 (Fighting Money
Laundering and Terrorist Financing), in particular Article 4 thereof;
Pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 347 of 6 August 2001 (Regulating the Money
Changer Profession in Lebanon), in particular Article 13 thereof;
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 7818 of 18 May 2001 and its
amendments (Regulations on the Control of Financial and Banking Operations for
Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing);
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 7933 of 27 September 2001
(Implementation Rules of the Law Regulating the Money Changer Profession);
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 7548 of 30 March 2000 and its
amendments (Electronic Financial and Banking Operations); and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, taken in its
meeting of 12 November 2025,
Decides the following:
Article 12: Definitions
For the purposes of this Decision, the following terms shall have the meanings hereunder
assigned to them:
- Non-Banking Financial Institutions (NBFIs): financial institutions, specialized
lending entities (comptoirs), exchange institutions, and Electronic Payment
Services Providers regulated by the Banque du Liban.
- Cash Transactions: any transaction in which a cash amount equal to, or above
USD 1,000 is deposited, withdrawn, paid, or received by a natural person or legal
entity (e.g., E-money, electronic money transfer, lending, currency exchange, and
collection services).
1- This title was amended pursuant to Article 1 of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026
(Intermediate Circular No. 761) that comes into force as of 30 June 2026.
2- This Article was amended pursuant to Article 2 of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026
(Intermediate Circular No. 761) that comes into force as of 30 June 2026.

Article 22: Scope of Implementation
In accordance with applicable regulations, the BDL directives, and AML/CFT international
standards, and with a view to prevent the misuse of the licensed financial system in
suspicious or high-risk operations, NBFIs are required to:
1. Collect, verify, record, and store systematically all information and data related to
customers and transactions.
2. Develop and implement effective policies and procedures in order to detect unusual or
suspicious transactions, particularly recurring transactions suspected of being aimed at
circumventing the designated threshold for cash transactions.
Article 31: Monitoring of Transactions
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1. Apply a USD 1,000 threshold or its equivalent on a transactional basis.
2. Flag recurring transactions whose apparent aim is to circumvent this threshold, and
take the necessary measures to detect and address them.
3. Abide by the AML/CFT policies and procedures in place at the Institution, and by the
obligation to report suspicious transactions as per applicable regulations.
Article 41: Forms RF1-A and RF1-B and their Completion
When adopting the two Forms for Cash Transactions, NBFIs are required to comply with the
following:
1. Complete Form RF1-A when carrying out any cash transaction equal to, or above
USD 1,000 or its equivalent. This Form shall be completed once by the concerned
customer, and updated periodically according to the customer's risk category,
provided that the update does not exceed five years for any customer.
2. Complete Form RF1-B when carrying out any cash transaction equal to, or above
USD 1,000 or its equivalent, on a transactional basis, except for cash withdrawals.
Both Forms shall be retained for at least five years.
3. Forms RF1-A and RF1-B shall be signed physically by both the customer and the
Institution.
4. Forms RF1-A and RF1-B may be signed electronically by the customer who is a
natural person, as per the electronic signature conditions specified in both Basic
Decision No. 13790 of 9 January 2026 and Basic Decision No. 7548 of 30 March
2000, provided that the value of the cash transaction or the total value of recurring
transactions by the same customer at the concerned institution does not exceed a
monthly amount of USD 10,000.
1- This Article was amended pursuant to Article 2 of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026
(Intermediate Circular No. 761) that comes into force as of 30 June 2026.

Article 51: Identity Verification and Source of Funds
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1- Verify the identity of the customer for each cash transaction, and keep a copy of a
valid identification document bearing their photo.
2- Update the identification document upon expiry.
3- Identify the source of funds without requiring the customer to provide supporting
documentation, unless:
- The value of the cash transaction or the total value of recurring transactions by the
same customer at the concerned institution is equal to, or above USD 10,000 or its
equivalent, per month.
- There are suspicions regarding the cash transaction, or the nature of the
transaction is inconsistent with the information provided in Form RF1-A.
Article 61: Record-Keeping and Reporting
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1. Securely store all information and documents related to cash transactions for at
least five years.
2. Submit to the Banque du Liban, within two business days, daily reports (a
separate report for each day) via the email (fx-curr-rf1@bdl.gov.lb), as per the
attached Form (Daily Transactions Report) prepared in Excel format, available at
the following link: Click to download.
Article 71: Sanctions
Any person that violates the provisions of this Decision shall incur the administrative
sanctions specified in Article 208 of the Code of Money and Credit. The infringing
institution shall also incur daily delay penalties calculated in US dollars and fixed by the
Central Council. Furthermore, the violation of the provisions of this Decision shall
constitute an offense under Article 770 of the Penal Code, and the Banque du Liban may
pursue any infringing institution before the competent judicial authority.
Article 8: This Decision shall come into force upon its issuance.
Article 9: This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, on 14 November 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
1- This Article was amended pursuant to Article 2 of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026
(Intermediate Circular No. 761) that comes into force as of 30 June 2026.
